name: Project Explore 2
instructions: The student is a Lithuanian school student (about 10-13 years old) and may have special educational needs. Speak to the student in simple, short, correct Lithuanian. English is only for the words, examples and practice. Keep English sentences very short and simple. Start every correction with 'Nedidelė klaidelė:', then show the correct English sentence and explain the mistake in one short Lithuanian sentence. Always ask the student to answer in a full sentence ('My cat is brown.', not 'brown'). Be warm and patient; praise effort. Ordinary body parts (head, arm, knee) are fine when the lesson needs them; never talk about private parts, romance, dating, alcohol, violence or anything really scary. Monsters and ghosts from the lesson are fine, in a fun way. Never ask for personal details such as addresses, phone numbers, school names or passwords.

grammar.name: have got / has got – turiu
grammar.explain: Have got reiškia „turėti“. Su he/she/it – has got. Neiginys: haven't got / hasn't got.
grammar.pattern: I have got (I've got) · She has got (She's got) · Have you got …? – Yes, I have.

examples.text: I've got a big bedroom.
Has he got a dog? – No, he hasn't.

exercises.q: I ___ got a big bedroom. (have / has)
Have they got a car? – Yes, they ___.

grammar.name: Present simple + adverbs of frequency
grammar.explain: Present simple – tai, ką darai įprastai. Su he/she/it veiksmažodis gauna -s. Kaip dažnai: always, usually, often, sometimes, hardly ever, never (prieš veiksmažodį).
grammar.pattern: I usually play … · She often wears … · He hardly ever …

examples.text: She usually wears glasses.
My friend hardly ever plays sport.

exercises.q: My friend ___ ever plays sport. (beveik niekada)

a: My friend hardly ever plays sport.
My friend hardly ever does sport.

grammar.name: Present simple ir continuous; stative verbs
grammar.explain: Present simple – įprasti dalykai, present continuous – tai, kas vyksta dabar. Kai kurie veiksmažodžiai (know, like, love, want, need, understand, believe) beveik niekada negauna -ing.
grammar.pattern: I live in … but I'm staying in … now. · I know (ne: I'm knowing)

examples.text: We usually live in a city, but now we're living in a tent.
examples.meaning: Paprastai gyvename mieste, bet dabar gyvename palapinėje.

examples.text: I understand you.

exercises.q: We usually live in a city, but now we ___ in a tent. (live / are living)
She ___ a new phone. (wants / is wanting)
Look! They ___ in the rainforest. (walk / are walking)

a: We're living in a tent now.
Now we're living in a tent.

grammar.name: Past simple: taisyklingi veiksmažodžiai
grammar.explain: Praeityje taisyklingi veiksmažodžiai gauna -ed: rain → rained, stay → stayed, stop → stopped, try → tried.
grammar.pattern: veiksmažodis + -ed

examples.text: It rained all day yesterday.
We stayed at home.

grammar.name: there was / there were
grammar.explain: Praeityje: there was – apie vieną, there were – apie kelis.
grammar.pattern: There was a … · There were some … · Was there …?

examples.text: There was a storm last night.
There were a lot of clouds.

exercises.q: There ___ a storm last night. (was / were)
There ___ a lot of clouds. (was / were)
Were there any people? – No, there ___.

a: There were a lot of clouds.

grammar.name: Prepositions of time – in / on / at
grammar.explain: In – mėnesiai, metai, metų laikai, dienos dalys (in July, in the morning). On – dienos ir datos (on Monday, on 5th May). At – laikas (at 7 o'clock, at the weekend).
grammar.pattern: in July · on Monday · at 3 o'clock

examples.text: It snowed in January.
We met on Saturday at 10 o'clock.

exercises.q: The film starts ___ seven o'clock. (in / on / at)
I get up early ___ the morning. (in / on / at)
My birthday is ___ the fifth of May. (in / on / at)

a: The lesson starts at eight o'clock.
The lesson begins at eight o'clock.

grammar.name: Past simple: netaisyklingi veiksmažodžiai
grammar.explain: Kai kurie veiksmažodžiai praeityje turi savo formą, ją reikia išmokti: buy → bought, eat → ate, drink → drank, give → gave, make → made, take → took, write → wrote, wear → wore.

examples.text: We ate some cheese and took a photo.

grammar.name: Comparative adjectives; (not) as … as
grammar.explain: Trumpi būdvardžiai: -er than (bigger than). Ilgi: more … than. As … as – „toks pat kaip“, not as … as – „ne toks kaip“.
grammar.pattern: bigger than · more beautiful than · as big as · not as old as

examples.text: The tower is taller than the cathedral.
The park isn't as big as the stadium.
examples.meaning: Parkas nėra toks didelis kaip stadionas.

a: The tower is taller than the cathedral.

grammar.name: Superlative adjectives
grammar.explain: Trumpi būdvardžiai: the …-est (the highest). Ilgi: the most … (the most beautiful). Išimtys: good → the best, bad → the worst, far → the furthest.
grammar.pattern: the + …-est · the most + būdvardis

examples.text: This is the highest hill.
It's the most beautiful view.

grammar.name: Articles: the, a / an
grammar.explain: A/an – kai kalbame apie daiktą pirmą kartą arba bet kurį (a museum). The – kai aišku, apie kurį kalbame, arba jis vienintelis (the museum next to the park).
grammar.pattern: There's a café. The café is next to the bank.

examples.text: There's an aquarium near the port.
The aquarium is opposite the town hall.

exercises.q: There's ___ aquarium near the port. (a / an)
There's a café. ___ café is next to the bank. (A / The)
I saw ___ dolphin in the harbour. (a / an)

a: There's an aquarium near the port.
The aquarium is opposite the town hall.
